title: Technology-Induced Discovery Clustering
summary: Tests whether general-purpose problem-solving technologies produce delayed, learning-mediated clusters of mathematical and scientific discovery.

hypotheses.statement: General-purpose problem-solving technologies produce statistically detectable, temporally concentrated increases in technology-dependent discovery after an adoption and method-learning lag.
falsification_conditions: No reproducible clustering remains after controlling for publication and researcher growth.
Detected peaks precede effective technology exposure.
Placebo dates and weakly compatible fields produce comparable effects.

hypotheses.statement: Candidate generation increases before accepted knowledge where verification or institutional acceptance capacity is constrained.
falsification_conditions: Candidate generation and accepted knowledge show no measurable divergence under verification constraints.

revision_history.change: Registered first pilot topic and linked progressive Site publication.

publication.status: published as pilot research; not confirmatory
